# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant o…

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — GitHub-issues machine runner (TEMPLATE).
#
# Copy into the TARGET repository (.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml) and
# adapt the RUNNER_* entries. This is the trimmed generic variant of the
# battle-tested machine-kit workflow (see epam/dmtools-dart
# .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml for the full reference with comments).
#
# Two entry paths, and BOTH must survive for the loop to be self-healing:
#   1. issues: [assigned, labeled] — the fast path (labels added with a
#      real PAT fire events; GITHUB_TOKEN-added labels do NOT — that is
#      exactly what the SM cron covers)
#   2. workflow_dispatch (issue / leg / reason) — the SM dispatch path:
#      the reconciler fires this directly, so mute labels cannot stall the
#      loop
#
# The guard derives the leg: dispatch input leg > label agent:rework >
# label agent:review > assignee/agent:dev (dev). Each leg runs the dmtools
# agent config named by RUNNER_*: dev (story/bug) develops from the issue
# body, review produces a machine PR review verdict, rework fixes the
# linked PR by the review threads.
name: 'AI Teammate'

# Run title carries the EFFECTIVE anchor (owner 2026-09-27, live: dmd run
# 36333172145): a PR-anchored SM dispatch (#544/#687 — inputs.pr set,
# inputs.issue empty) must title '▶ rework (SM) · pr-266', never the
# malformed '▶ rework (SM) · gh- · gh-: '. (inputs.pr || '') guards the
# label-event path, where inputs are null — null != '' would be TRUE and
# render 'pr-' for ordinary issue events.
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (#544/#687) — the SM dispatches review/rework with pr instead of issue when the PR has no resolvable LOCAL issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: write

env:
  AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
  # ── adapt per target repo ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  RUNNER_STORY: dmtools-agents/story_development.json
  RUNNER_BUG: dmtools-agents/bug_development.json
  RUNNER_REVIEW: dmtools-agents/pr_review.json
  RUNNER_REWORK: dmtools-agents/pr_rework.json
  DMTOOLS_AGENTS_REF: main
  DMTOOLS_VERSION: v0.1.5
  FA_VERSION: latest
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Secrets expected: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT), plus the AI provider key
  # referenced by the runner configs (e.g. ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY).

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
    steps:
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            LABELS="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')"
            ASSIGNEES="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"
          fi
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state)"
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          if [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "rework" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "review" ]; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif [ "$INPUT_LEG" = "dev" ]; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework"; then runner="$RUNNER_REWORK";
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW";
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$(echo "$runner" | grep -q review && echo review || (echo "$runner" | grep -q rework && echo rework || echo dev))" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      # Adapt the runner steps from the machine-kit reference workflow:
      # checkout (target + dmtools-agents), install dmtools + fa, write the
      # issue body to input/ticket.md, then:
      #   dmtools run "$RUNNER" '{"params":{"ticketKey":"gh-<n>"}}'
      # Full working reference: epam/dmtools-dart .github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml
      - run: echo "Adapt runner steps from the machine-kit reference (see header comment)"

env:

jobs:

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)

# Factory · AI Teammate leg — REUSABLE workflow (dmtools-agents factory pack, top-level: GitHub requires reusable workflows at the .github/workflows root — no subdirectories).
#
# The dev→review→rework machine loop for GitHub-issues trackers, hosted in
# dmtools-agents so target repositories carry only a thin stub (event
# triggers + this call) plus .dmtools/config.js, secrets and vars. Runs in
# the CALLER's context: github.repository = the target repo; vars.* and
# secrets.* resolve from the caller (each target pins its own versions).
#
# Legs (guard derives the slot when `leg` is empty):
#   bug | story | review | rework — the runner configs live in the TARGET repo
#   (.dmtools/runners/*), wired via .dmtools/config.js sm.runners.
#
# Loop mechanics (identical to the dmtools-dart template this was ported
# from — see that file's history for the full rationale):
#   issue assigned/labeled → guard → ticket input → dmtools run <runner>
#   → agent develops → PR ("Closes #NN") → review verdict step:
#       APPROVE + green PR checks → pr_approved → merge (merge-trigger/stub)
#       CHANGES_REQUESTED        → agent:rework (bounded: MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS,
#                                  then needs-human escalation)
#   Review/rework queue labels are stripped at cycle end (no self-loops).
#   fa sessions ride the fa-sess/gh-<n> branch (cache saves are denied on
#   issues-event runs); fa project memory is committed back to the repo.
#
# Secrets (via `secrets: inherit`): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (PAT — labels added
#   with GITHUB_TOKEN never fire `labeled` events; pushes must not author
#   as github-actions[bot]), ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY.
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
#   MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS (default 2).
#
# Caller stub:
#   on:
#     issues: {types: [assigned, labeled]}
#     workflow_dispatch: {inputs: {issue: {type: number}, leg: {type: string}}}
#   concurrency:
#     group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#     cancel-in-progress: false
#   jobs:
#     factory:
#       uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>
#       with:
#         issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
#         leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
#         reason: ${{ inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
#       secrets: inherit

name: 'Factory · AI Teammate'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: 'Runner label (self-hosted pools must be visible to the CALLING org)'
        type: string
        default: 'ubuntu-24.04'
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (string: number-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions). Empty when pr is given (PR-anchored run, #687).'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687). Exactly one of issue|pr must be set.'
        required: false
        type: string
      machine-author:
        description: "Deployment's machine (bot) login (#687): gates rework re-arm in PR-anchored reviews (auto-approve via pr_approved is author-agnostic per the owner rule). Injected as jobParams.machineAuthor — branch-independent (the checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config)."
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: "Which leg to run: dev | review | rework (empty = derive from labels/assignees)"
        required: false
        type: string
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      factory_ref:
        description: 'The dmtools-agents ref the factory runs from (the literal in the stub uses-line). github.workflow_ref cannot serve: in a called workflow it carries the CALLER ref, not the uses-ref.'
        required: true
        type: string
      flutter-version:
        description: 'Flutter SDK for agent work (cached). "" skips — for pure-Dart targets that only need dart from the runner image. A value installs Flutter+matching Dart via flutter-action with SDK caching (e.g. "stable", "3.38.0").'
        required: false
        default: 'stable'
        type: string

    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN:
        description: 'PAT with repo scope — machine labels, pushes, PR/issue API (secrets: inherit does not cross repository boundaries).'
        required: true
      ZAI_CODE_KEY:
        description: 'z.ai API key (dev/rework provider + review queue fallback)'
        required: false
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY:
        description: 'kimi API key (review provider, first in the queue)'
        required: false

# NOTE: no `concurrency` here — the caller stub owns the per-issue group.
# A reusable workflow with the SAME group as its caller deadlocks: the caller
# holds the group while the called workflow waits for it forever (pending, 0 jobs).

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  # actions/cache@v6 save phase needs actions:write on github.token.
  actions: write

jobs:
  guard:
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.check.outputs.run }}
      runner: ${{ steps.check.outputs.runner }}
      config: ${{ steps.check.outputs.config }}
      kind: ${{ steps.check.outputs.kind }}
      anchor: ${{ steps.check.outputs.anchor }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository (config, runners)
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # caller-repo checkout: the factory reads .dmtools/config.js from
          # the TARGET repository, never from the factory pack
          ref: ${{ github.ref }}
          # gate job only: config.js at the head + API guards — no git
          # history walks. fetch-depth 0 cloned the FULL history here
          # (~1 min on fa, every leg) for nothing.
          fetch-depth: 1
      - name: Decide whether this event is for the agent
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          # Event context rides through from the caller (issues events) —
          # empty for pure dispatches. The guard ALWAYS refreshes from the
          # API (queued runs see a stale payload); this is only a fallback.
          ASSIGNEES: ${{ join(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, ' ') }}
          LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, ' ') }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.action || github.event_name }}
          # #544: the `labeled` event sender — the owner-override gate checks
          # its repo permission before honoring a manual agent:rework.
          # Empty for schedule-scan dispatches (SM ticks): the label is
          # trusted as-is there (see rework_override_ok below).
          SENDER: ${{ github.event.sender.login || '' }}
          INPUT_LEG: ${{ inputs.leg }}
          INPUT_REASON: ${{ inputs.reason }}
          # The assignee gate below compares against the machine login.
          # AGENT_HANDLE lives on the TEAMMATE job's env — without it here
          # the guard's $AGENT_HANDLE is empty, `grep -w` never matches, and
          # assignment-triggered dev legs never start (live: dmtools-dart
          # run 35519287617 — issue #173 assigned to ai-teammate → skipped).
          AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
        run: |
          # Anchor validation (#687): exactly one of issue|pr.
          if [ -n "$NUMBER" ] && [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            echo "::error::both issue ($NUMBER) and pr ($PR_NUMBER) given — exactly one anchor allowed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$NUMBER" ] && [ -z "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            echo "::error::no anchor — pass either issue or pr"
            exit 1
          fi

          # ── runners come from the TARGET repo (.dmtools/config.js) ──
          # The factory ships no repo-specific runners: sm.runners maps
          # legs to configs in this repository (see the integration guide,
          # "Overriding agents per repository"). dev covers bug and story.
          if [ ! -f .dmtools/config.js ]; then
            echo "::error::.dmtools/config.js not found — the factory needs sm.runners to know this repo's agents (docs/machine-factory-integration.md §5a)"
            exit 1
          fi
          ovr="$(node -e "try{const c=require('./.dmtools/config.js');const r=(c.sm&&c.sm.runners)||{};console.log([r.bug||r.dev||'',r.story||r.dev||'',r.review||'',r.rework||''].join('\t'))}catch(e){}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$ovr" ]; then
            echo "::error::sm.runners missing in .dmtools/config.js (bug/story[/dev], review, rework → runner config paths)"
            exit 1
          fi
          RUNNER_BUG="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f1)"
          RUNNER_STORY="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f2)"
          RUNNER_REVIEW="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f3)"
          RUNNER_REWORK="$(echo "$ovr" | cut -f4)"
          echo "→ runners (from .dmtools/config.js): bug=${RUNNER_BUG:--} story=${RUNNER_STORY:--} review=${RUNNER_REVIEW:--} rework=${RUNNER_REWORK:--}"

          # Owner override gate (#544 owner rule, issue comment 3): a MANUAL
          # agent:rework label IS the explicit override — it fires rework on
          # ANY PR (machine or guest, with or without a local issue). But the
          # machine NEVER self-triggers rework on guest PRs, and a random
          # external labeler must not burn factory tokens. Where the
          # `labeled` event sender is known, gate the override on its repo
          # permission (write/admin/maintain). Schedule-scan dispatches and
          # non-labeled events carry no meaningful actor — the label is
          # trusted as-is (the SM consumed/verified it upstream).
          rework_override_ok() {
            if [ "$ACTOR" != "labeled" ] || [ -z "$SENDER" ]; then
              return 0
            fi
            perm="$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/collaborators/$SENDER/permission" -q .permission 2>/dev/null || true)"
            case "$perm" in
              admin|maintain|write) return 0 ;;
              *)
                echo "::warning::agent:rework by '$SENDER' (permission: ${perm:-none}) — the owner override requires write/admin; skipping (never fails the cycle, #544)"
                return 1
                ;;
            esac
          }

          # ── PR-anchored dispatch (#687): the PR is the anchor. Review was
          # the only leg defined for it — #544 extends the branch to REWORK:
          # a labeled PR with no resolvable LOCAL issue anchors on the PR
          # itself (pr-<N>, owner rule 3) and the rework runner derives its
          # context from the PR (review findings, failing checks).
          if [ -n "$PR_NUMBER" ]; then
            state="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$state" ]; then
              # #544 rule 2: an unresolvable anchor is a warn-and-skip —
              # never exit 1. One bad number must not stall the machine loop.
              echo "::warning::PR #$PR_NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY — skipping (clean no-op, #544)"
              echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
            if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
              echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
              exit 0
            fi
            # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the freeze switch applies to
            # PR-anchored legs too — a frozen PR gets no review/rework run.
            pr_blocked="$(gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --json labels -q '([.labels[].name] | index("blocked")) != null' 2>/dev/null || echo false)"
            if [ "$pr_blocked" = "true" ]; then
              echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "→ PR #$PR_NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
              exit 0
            fi
            leg="$INPUT_LEG"
            if [ -z "$leg" ] && echo "$INPUT_REASON" | grep -qi 'rework'; then
              leg="rework"
            fi
            if [ "$leg" = "rework" ]; then
              if ! rework_override_ok; then
                echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "runner=$RUNNER_REWORK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "config=factory-agents/pr_rework.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "kind=rework" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "→ PR-anchored REWORK of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}, #544)"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$RUNNER_REVIEW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "config=factory-agents/pr_review.json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=review" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "anchor=pr-${PR_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ PR-anchored review of #$PR_NUMBER (reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>})"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "anchor=gh-${NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # ALWAYS refresh labels/assignees from the API — not just for
          # explicit dispatches. Event-triggered runs (issues:assigned,
          # labeled, ...) sit QUEUED behind the per-issue concurrency group,
          # and the github.event.issue payload they carry is a snapshot from
          # trigger time: a guard that trusts it misses labels the
          # already-running leg has since applied (status:In Development,
          # status:In Rework) and dispatches a duplicate dev/rework leg on
          # top of the live one (live: dmtools-dart run 36252718919 for #257;
          # a duplicate rework dispatch for #259). The event payload is only
          # a fallback when the API read itself fails.
          if fresh_labels="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json labels -q '[.labels[].name] | join(" ")')" \
            && fresh_assignees="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json assignees -q '[.assignees[].login] | join(" ")')"; then
            LABELS="$fresh_labels"
            ASSIGNEES="$fresh_assignees"
          else
            echo "::warning::labels/assignees refresh failed for #$NUMBER — falling back to the (possibly stale) event payload"
          fi
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            echo "→ dispatch: leg=$INPUT_LEG reason=${INPUT_REASON:-<none>}"
          fi
          # Closed issues are terminal: no agent runs on them. #544 rule 2:
          # a FAILED resolution (404 — missing issue or cross-repo ref like
          # 'dm.ai #601') is a warn-and-skip, never exit 1 — one bad anchor
          # must not turn the whole SM cycle red every 15 min.
          state="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json state -q .state 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$state" ]; then
            echo "::warning::issue #$NUMBER could not be resolved in $GITHUB_REPOSITORY (missing or cross-repo ref) — skipping this leg (clean no-op, #544)"
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$state" != "OPEN" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ issue #$NUMBER is ${state} — not for the agent"
            exit 0
          fi
          # agent:skip — hard opt-out for smoke/verification tickets.
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:skip"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ issue #$NUMBER carries agent:skip — agent bypassed"
            exit 0
          fi
          # 'blocked' = human hold (fa #939): the official freeze switch —
          # no leg starts on a frozen item, whatever the event (assignment,
          # any label echo). Same label the SM engine and the machine-SM
          # reconciler honor; removing it returns the item to the loop.
          if echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "blocked"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ issue #$NUMBER carries blocked — human hold, the machine skips it entirely"
            exit 0
          fi
          runner=""
          slot=""
          if [ -n "$INPUT_LEG" ]; then
            case "$INPUT_LEG" in
              rework) runner="$RUNNER_REWORK"; slot="rework" ;;
              review) runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review" ;;
              dev)
                title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
                if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' \
                  || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
                  runner="$RUNNER_BUG"; slot="bug"
                else
                  runner="$RUNNER_STORY"; slot="story"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework" \
            && ! echo "$LABELS" | grep -q 'status:In Rework'; then
            # status:In Rework = a rework leg already runs/ran — its own
            # status transition echoes back as a `labeled` event and would
            # re-derive the same leg on top of itself.
            # #544: manual agent:rework is the owner override — it fires
            # rework even from a `labeled` event, but only when the labeler
            # has write/admin (see rework_override_ok). Without permission
            # the override is ignored (runner stays empty → clean skip).
            if rework_override_ok; then
              runner="$RUNNER_REWORK"
            fi
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then
            # status:In Review is NOT an in-flight marker here — the DEV leg
            # sets it as the "ready for review" invitation, so blocking on it
            # kills the label-echo review trigger (live: dmtools-dart gh-182).
            # Real duplicate protection is the per-issue concurrency group.
            runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review"
          elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qE 'status:In Development|status:In Review|status:In Rework|in progress|ai_developed|ai_pr_reviewed|_wip|rework-round-'; then
            # Dev is a FRESH handoff only: once the loop has touched the
            # issue, later `labeled` events (the dev leg's OWN status:In
            # Development transition, SM backfill labels, ...) would
            # re-derive dev and queue a duplicate leg on top of the
            # running/finished one (live: fa gh-746 — the assigned-handoff
            # dev ran while its status-label echo queued a second dev).
            # The SM owns the loop from there; explicit dispatches
            # (inputs.leg) bypass this derive branch entirely.
            :
          elif echo "$ASSIGNEES" | grep -qw "$AGENT_HANDLE" \
            || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:dev"; then
            title="$(gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json title -q .title)"
            if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' \
              || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
              runner="$RUNNER_BUG"; slot="bug"
            else
              runner="$RUNNER_STORY"; slot="story"
            fi
          fi
          if [ -n "$runner" ]; then
            # Parent agent config — fa-session.sh derives the session group
            # from its basename (dev-write vs dev-review).
            # Parent pipeline by SLOT — custom runners (config overrides)
            # inherit the leg's pipeline, so a repo can swap the agent
            # without losing session/verdict semantics. The value below is
            # the LEGACY tree path; the teammate job re-resolves it pack-first
            # (Wave 2: an unpacked pack's launch.json WINS — see the
            # "Resolve parent config" step; this fallback keeps old pins
            # working when no Wave-2 pack is unpacked).
            case "$slot" in
              bug)     config="factory-agents/bug_development.json"; kind="dev" ;;
              story)   config="factory-agents/story_development.json"; kind="dev" ;;
              review)  config="factory-agents/pr_review.json";        kind="review" ;;
              rework)  config="factory-agents/pr_rework.json";        kind="dev" ;;
              *)       config="factory-agents/story_development.json"; kind="dev" ;;
            esac
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "runner=$runner" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "config=$config" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "kind=$kind" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ agent run: $runner (event=$ACTOR, labels=$LABELS, assignees=$ASSIGNEES)"
          else
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "→ not for the agent (event=$ACTOR, labels=$LABELS, assignees=$ASSIGNEES)"
          fi

  teammate:
    needs: guard
    if: needs.guard.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
    # A real fix is a 40-80 minute agent session (gh-623 burned a full RCA +
    # TDD cycle at exactly 61 minutes and the job was killed mid-work); dev
    # legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + full flutter test suite
    # and live 2-3 hours (fa gh-1077 leg was killed mid-work at exactly 110
    # on 2026-09-30). The autocommit timer (300s) bounds the blast radius of
    # a kill; this timeout bounds the bill.
    timeout-minutes: 260
    # Workflow-level env is NOT supported in reusable (workflow_call)
    # workflows — the factory failed validation at startup until this
    # moved down to the job.
    env:
      AGENT_HANDLE: ai-teammate
      FA_VERSION: ${{ vars.FA_VERSION_MACHINE || vars.FA_VERSION || 'latest' }}
      DMTOOLS_VERSION: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION || 'v0.1.14' }}
      MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS: ${{ vars.MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS || 2 }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout target repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The engine and glue ride the factory-setup zip (releases) and
          # the agent packs (registry) — but parent runner configs may
          # reference the target's submodule paths verbatim
          # (agents/js/*.js, ./agents/scripts/*) so the machine runs
          # identically locally and in the factory — the submodule MUST be
          # initialized at the reviewed, pinned SHA.
          submodules: true
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Resolve factory ref (self-pin)
        # github.workflow_ref = "<owner>/<repo>/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@<ref>"
        # — runners, scripts and workflow are checked out at EXACTLY the ref
        # the caller invoked: engine and factory can never skew apart.
        run: |
          # The stub passes the same literal its uses-line pins — engine and
          # factory can never skew apart. Keep both in sync when flipping refs.
          echo "FACTORY_REF=${{ inputs.factory_ref }}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: "Fetch factory-setup (dmtools-agents releases — no tree checkout)"
        # Owner mandate 2026-10-03: the factory NEVER clones the
        # dmtools-agents tree. The workflow glue the run needs —
        # setup/ toolbelt (install.sh, cache.sh, review-verdict.sh,
        # fa-session.sh, ...), scripts/git-push-guard.sh fallback and the
        # four legacy leg configs — ships as the factory-setup-*.zip
        # release asset (built by ci/release_packs.mjs, rides every
        # agents-rel-* tag).
        # Compat: a pre-mounted factory-agents/ tree still WINS over the
        # zip — hosts that intentionally mount the tree (dmtools-agents'
        # own factory-probe, forks pinning local trees) keep their copies.
        # FACTORY_ROOT carries the winner for every later step.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PACK_TAG: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          # Compat branch: mounted tree wins, untouched.
          if [ -d "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/factory-agents" ]; then
            echo "→ compat: factory-agents/ tree is mounted — it wins (FACTORY_ROOT=tree)"
            echo "FACTORY_ROOT=${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/factory-agents" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            exit 0
          fi
          # DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY is the dm.ai #579 RESOLVER format — a
          # releases BASE URL (…/releases/latest/download) or a tag URL;
          # only a bare tag can feed `gh release download` directly.
          tag="${PACK_TAG}"
          case "${tag}" in
            http*)
              # …/releases/tag/<tag> pins exactly; anything else (/latest/,
              # /download/) resolves to the newest agents-rel-* tag.
              pinned="$(printf '%s' "${tag}" | sed -n 's#.*/releases/tag/\([A-Za-z0-9._-]\+\).*#\1#p')"
              if [ -n "${pinned}" ] && printf '%s' "${pinned}" | grep -q '^agents-rel-'; then
                tag="${pinned}"
              else
                tag=""
              fi
              ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "${tag}" ]; then
            tag="$(gh release list --repo IstiN/dmtools-agents --limit 10 --json tagName \
              --jq '[.[].tagName | select(startswith("agents-rel-"))] | .[0]')"
            [ -n "${tag}" ] || { echo "::error::no agents-rel-* release found in IstiN/dmtools-agents"; exit 1; }
            echo "::notice::factory-setup from newest release ${tag}"
          fi
          dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-setup"
          mkdir -p "${dir}"
          tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
          gh release download "${tag}" --repo IstiN/dmtools-agents \
            --pattern 'factory-setup-*.zip' --dir "${tmp}" --clobber
          unzip -q "${tmp}"/factory-setup-*.zip -d "${dir}"
          [ -f "${dir}/setup/cache.sh" ] || { echo "::error::factory-setup incomplete at ${tag} (no setup/cache.sh)"; exit 1; }
          [ -f "${dir}/configs/pr_review.json" ] || { echo "::error::factory-setup incomplete at ${tag} (no configs/)"; exit 1; }
          echo "→ factory-setup from ${tag} (FACTORY_ROOT=${dir})"
          echo "FACTORY_ROOT=${dir}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: "Fetch factory kit (this repo @ invocation ref — immutable)"
        # Trust-boundary scripts (git push guard, source PAT credentials)
        # ride the SAME immutable ref the caller invoked this workflow at
        # (github.workflow_ref = owner/repo/.github/workflows/<name>.yml@<ref>)
        # — a PR head can no longer supply them (self-host security,
        # 2026-10-01) and the script version can never skew from the workflow
        # version that calls it. Plain git (no action): GitLab-portable.
        #
        # RUNNER_TEMP, never $GITHUB_WORKSPACE: a nested git repo inside the
        # workspace poisons every downstream `git add` (the gitlink "does
        # not have a commit checked out", exit 128 — live fa gh-1000
        # 2026-10-03: PR staging, origin-sync clean-tree gate, and the
        # session timer auto-commit all tripped on it).
        env:
          AWF_REF: ${{ github.workflow_ref }}
        run: |
          ref="${AWF_REF##*@}"
          dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit"
          git init -q "$dir"
          git -C "$dir" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows.git
          git -C "$dir" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$ref" \
            || { echo "::warning::kit fetch failed — falling back to FACTORY_ROOT copies"; exit 0; }
          git -C "$dir" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD -- kit/
          [ -f "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" ] || { echo "::warning::kit incomplete at $ref — falling back"; rm -rf "$dir"; exit 0; }
          # Kit liveness probe (awf#7): a guard whose shebang is not line 1
          # silently executes under /bin/sh and dies with "Syntax error" on
          # every git call — the whole dev session loses git (branch setup,
          # timer auto-commit, PR post-action) with quiet skips downstream.
          head -1 "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" | grep -q '^#!.*bash' \
            || { echo "::error::kit git-push-guard.sh lost its shebang (line 1) at $ref — refusing to arm a broken guard"; exit 1; }
          cp "$dir/kit/git-push-guard.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe" && chmod +x "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/git-probe" version >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || { echo "::error::kit git-push-guard.sh does not execute (probe failed) at $ref"; exit 1; }

      - name: "Resolve parent config (pack launch.json wins, tree fallback)"
        # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): teammate packs are self-sufficient —
        # the unpacked pack's launch.json IS the launch contract and WINS
        # over the legacy tree copy. Pack cache root (dmtools
        # AgentPackResolver): ~/.dmtools/packs/<agent>-<version>/ —
        # populated by `dmtools run` resolving a <agent>@latest parent, so
        # it is visible here on persistent-HOME/self-hosted runners and to
        # every step AFTER the agent run; fresh hosted runners fall back to
        # the legacy tree config until the run unpacks the pack. Neither
        # source present ⇒ loud fail (old pin without tree configs and
        # without a Wave-2 pack). fa-session.sh/run-agent.sh derive the
        # agent identity from the pack DIR, so naming stays stable either
        # way. Plain bash: GitLab-portable.
        env:
          LEGACY_CONFIG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.config }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          agent="$(basename "${LEGACY_CONFIG}" .json)"
          pack_launch="$(ls -1 "${HOME}"/.dmtools/packs/"${agent}"-*/launch.json 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1 || true)"
          if [ -n "${pack_launch}" ]; then
            echo "→ pack launch.json wins: ${pack_launch}"
            echo "AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE=${pack_launch}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            exit 0
          fi
          # No unpacked pack — the legacy fallback now lives under
          # FACTORY_ROOT: a mounted tree keeps its root-level <agent>.json
          # layout; the factory-setup zip ships configs/<agent>.json.
          for legacy_path in \
            "${FACTORY_ROOT}/${agent}.json" \
            "${FACTORY_ROOT}/configs/${agent}.json"; do
            if [ -f "${legacy_path}" ]; then
              echo "→ no unpacked ${agent} pack launch.json — legacy config: ${legacy_path}"
              echo "AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE=${legacy_path}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
              exit 0
            fi
          done
          echo "::error::no parent config for '${agent}': neither ~/.dmtools/packs/${agent}-*/launch.json nor ${FACTORY_ROOT}/${agent}.json nor ${FACTORY_ROOT}/configs/${agent}.json exists — no Wave-2 pack unpacked and the factory-setup legacy configs are missing"
          exit 1

      - name: Export fa session identity + cache keys
        # AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE comes from the resolve step above
        # (pack launch.json wins) via GITHUB_ENV.
        env:
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        run: bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/cache.sh" keys fa-session

      - name: Restore fa session (resume the ticket conversation)
        # actions/cache saves are denied on issues-event runs (job token is
        # cache-read-only there), so the session tree rides a dedicated git
        # branch per issue; the per-issue concurrency group serializes writers.
        env:
          FA_SESS_BRANCH: fa-sess/${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
        run: |
          if git fetch --depth 1 origin "refs/heads/$FA_SESS_BRANCH"; then
            git checkout "refs/remotes/origin/$FA_SESS_BRANCH" -- .dmtools/fa-sessions
            # Unstage (checkout <ref> -- <path> STAGES): the session store
            # belongs on the fa-sess branch only.
            git restore --staged .dmtools/fa-sessions
            echo "→ fa session restored from $FA_SESS_BRANCH"
          else
            echo "→ no saved fa session yet ($FA_SESS_BRANCH absent) — starting fresh"
          fi

      - name: Cache fa CLI (by version)
        if: env.FA_VERSION != 'latest'
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.local/bin/fa
            ~/lib
          key: fa-${{ env.FA_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: Resolve dmtools CLI version (latest -> current tag)
        # 'latest' (or empty) resolves to the current release tag so the
        # version-locked install.sh URL keeps working; owner mandate
        # 2026-10-01: machine legs always track the latest CLI/agents.
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION:-}" = "latest" ]; then
            TAG="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "DMTOOLS_VERSION=${TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
            echo "::notice::dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${TAG}"
          fi

      - name: Cache dmtools CLI (by version)
        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.dmtools/bin
          key: dmtools-${{ env.DMTOOLS_VERSION }}-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}

      - name: "Install prerequisites (fa; no-op on cache hit)"
        # Authenticated gh api download first — anonymous release-asset
        # downloads hit GitHub edge caches that served stale 404s for hours
        # after a re-cut release (observed 2026-09-12).
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if ! command -v fa >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ ! -x "${HOME}/.local/bin/fa" ]; then
            case "$(uname -m)" in
              x86_64) FA_ARCH="x64" ;;
              *)      FA_ARCH="arm64" ;;
            esac
            tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
            # 'latest' is a WORD, not a tag — gh release download takes a
            # literal tag; with no tag it resolves the latest release.
            # (Live failure on IstiN/flutter_agent_harness gh-623: the repo
            # has no FA_VERSION var -> 'latest' -> "release not found".)
            # A fresh latest release can also be asset-less for a while
            # (v0.1.418 2026-09-18: tag landed, binaries never uploaded ->
            # review leg died "no assets to download"). Walk back to the
            # newest release that actually ships the CLI bundle.
            if [ "${FA_VERSION}" = "latest" ] || [ -z "${FA_VERSION}" ]; then
              for t in $(gh release list \
                  --repo IstiN/flutter_agent_harness --limit 10 \
                  --json tagName --jq '.[].tagName'); do
                if gh release view "$t" --repo IstiN/flutter_agent_harness \
                    --json assets --jq '.assets[].name' 2>/dev/null \
                    | grep -q "^fa-linux-${FA_ARCH}\.tar\.gz$"; then
                  FA_VERSION="$t"
                  echo "fa install: latest asset-less, falling back to ${FA_VERSION}"
                  break
                fi
              done
            fi
            gh release download "${FA_VERSION}" \
              --repo IstiN/flutter_agent_harness \
              --pattern "fa-linux-${FA_ARCH}.tar.gz" --dir "${tmp}" --clobber
            tar -xzf "${tmp}/fa-linux-${FA_ARCH}.tar.gz" -C "${tmp}"
            mkdir -p "${HOME}/.local/bin" "${HOME}/.local/lib"
            cp "${tmp}/bundle/bin/fa" "${HOME}/.local/bin/fa"
            chmod +x "${HOME}/.local/bin/fa"
            # version.txt next to the binary — _packageVersion probes
            # <exe_dir>/version.txt; without it the CLI reports the 0.1.0
            # fallback and every session reinstalls (2026-10-01 loop).
            [ -f "${tmp}/bundle/version.txt" ] \
              && cp "${tmp}/bundle/version.txt" "${HOME}/.local/bin/version.txt"
            cp -R "${tmp}/bundle/lib/." "${HOME}/.local/lib/" 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
          bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/install.sh" "fa:${FA_VERSION}"

      - name: Install dmtools CLI (pinned release bundle)
        # The installer ships as a release asset, version-locked to the
        # bundle it installs — no copy of install.sh in the target repo.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL "https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/releases/download/${DMTOOLS_VERSION}/install.sh" \
            -o /tmp/dmtools-install.sh
          bash /tmp/dmtools-install.sh "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # flutter-action treats a literal version string strictly — the words
      # stable/beta/main/master are CHANNELS and crash the action ("Unable
      # to determine Flutter version for channel: stable", live: gh-623 run
      # 35370007049). Two steps with plain if-comparisons — the GH parser
      # rejects map-indexing expressions inside with:.
      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (channel)
        if: inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master'
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          channel: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Set up Flutter for agent work (pinned version)
        if: inputs.flutter-version != '' && !(inputs.flutter-version == 'stable' || inputs.flutter-version == 'beta' || inputs.flutter-version == 'main' || inputs.flutter-version == 'master')
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: ${{ inputs.flutter-version }}
          cache: true

      - name: Verify prerequisites
        run: |
          fa --version
          dmtools --version
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.flutter-version }}" ]; then
            flutter --version
            dart --version
          fi

      - name: Configure Git Author + push credentials
        # Purge the checkout's App token and make SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN the
        # credential that wins for github.com pushes (all logic in the
        # shared installer — one copy serves every push path in the job).
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash "${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/kit/install-source-git-credentials.sh" 2>/dev/null \
            || bash "${FACTORY_ROOT}/setup/install-source-git-credentials.sh"

      - name: Trace git credential stack (push-time evidence)
        # gh-63 Task 1 — same run that pushes, right before the agent.
        # What each section proves:
        #   --show-origin        WHERE each credential source lives; the
        #                        extraheader section must come back empty —
        #                        asserted below, so any resurrection of the
        #                        App-token header (checkout layout change,
        #                        mid-run config write) fails the run here
        #                        instead of silently re-arming bot pushes
        #   submodule foreach    same proof for each submodule local config
        #                        (checkout arms those with submodules: true)
        #   git credential fill  dry-runs the exact push-path resolution and
        #                        shows the winning username; the password is
        #                        masked, and the helper's stderr line confirms
        #                        SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN served the credential
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p .dmtools
          echo "── credential.helper — all scopes, with origins ──"
          git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper || true
          git config --show-origin --get-all credential.https://github.com.helper || true
          echo "── http.https://github.com/.extraheader (must be empty — App token purged) ──"
          # Redact the VALUE (gh-63 review threads 11/12): on a leftover this
          # dump prints AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(App token)> — GitHub's
          # log masking matches the raw token string, not its base64 form.
          # git 2.x prints "<origin>\t<value>" (--show-origin --get-all has
          # NO key= prefix), so redact everything after the first TAB — a
          # sed on '=' alone would only trim the base64 padding. The origin
          # (file/scope) stays visible; a tab-less line is fully redacted.
          git config --show-origin --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader | sed -E 's/^([^\t]*\t).*/\1<redacted>/; t; s/.+/<redacted> (unexpected line without origin)/' || true
          if git config --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader | grep -q .; then
            echo "::error::App-token extraheader still present after purge — pushes would authenticate as github-actions[bot]"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "── submodule extraheaders (must be empty — App token purged there too) ──"
          # checkout arms every submodule's local config with the same token;
          # a push made from inside agents/ must not fall back to it (gh-63).
          # The probe echoes a LEFTOVER marker line only when a config is
          # still armed, so "no submodules" and "all clean" stay quiet.
          # The marker names the submodule but NEVER the header value: it is
          # AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64(App token)>, decodable and NOT masked
          # by GitHub log redaction (gh-63 review threads 11/12).
          sub_leftovers="$(git submodule foreach --quiet --recursive \
            'c="$(git config --get-all http.https://github.com/.extraheader || true)"; [ -z "$c" ] || echo "LEFTOVER ${sm_path}: <redacted>"' \
            || true)"
          if [ -n "$sub_leftovers" ]; then
            echo "::error::App-token extraheader still present in a submodule config after purge — pushes from inside the submodule would authenticate as github-actions[bot]"
            printf '%s\n' "$sub_leftovers"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "── commit identity ──"
          git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT
          git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT
          echo "── dry-run: credential a github.com push would use ──"
          # Capture first, then assert: with GIT_ASKPASS=echo `git credential
          # fill` exits 0 even when NO helper answered (echo prints its prompt
          # back, git accepts it as a bogus credential) — only the
          # SOURCE helper's username proves the SOURCE credential wins.
          # CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT tags the helper's log line so this dry-run
          # stays distinguishable from real pushes in the evidence log.
          out="$(printf 'protocol=https\nhost=github.com\n' | CRED_HELPER_CONTEXT=trace-dry-run GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=echo git credential fill 2>&1)" || true
          if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^username=x-access-token$'; then
            echo "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted — served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper>/'
          else
            echo "::error::dry-run credential was NOT served by the SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN helper — a github.com push would not authenticate as the SOURCE account"
            printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -E 's/^password=.+/password=<redacted>/'
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Seed local git excludes (factory workspace artifacts)
        # Everything the factory/agent scribbles into the workspace that must
        # NEVER reach a commit (agents run `git add -A`). .git/info/exclude is
        # local-only by construction — no .gitignore pollution in agent PRs.
        run: |
          {
            echo '# factory workspace artifacts (seeded per-run, never commit)'
            echo '.codegraph/'
            echo '.dmtools/fa-trace.log'
            echo '.dmtools/run-output.txt'
            echo '.dmtools/stall-capture.log'
            echo '.dmtools/fa-sessions/'
            echo '.dmtools/copilot-sessions/'
            echo '.fah/bash_jobs/'
            echo '# the factory clone itself: an in-index gitlink without'
            echo '# .gitmodules breaks every actions/checkout with submodules'
            echo 'factory-agents/'
          } >> .git/info/exclude

      - name: Write the issue into the agent input folder
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
        run: |
          # ticket.json carries the tracker-contract fields: dmtools hydrates
          # it into params.ticket for every JS action (Tracker abstraction).
          mkdir -p "input/gh-${NUMBER}"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json number,title,body,url,state,labels \
            -q '{key: ("gh-" + (.number|tostring)), number: .number,
                 title: .title, body: .body, url: .url, state: .state,
                 labels: [.labels[].name]}' \
            > "input/gh-${NUMBER}/ticket.json"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json title,body -q '.title, .body' > input/ticket.md
          echo "input/ticket.md: $(wc -l < input/ticket.md) lines"

      - name: Write the PR into the agent input folder (PR-anchored runs)
        # #687: the PR is the anchor — the pr-N contextId is what the agent
        # scripts key on; ticket.json carries the same tracker-contract
        # shape so hydration paths stay uniform.
        if: inputs.pr != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ inputs.pr }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "input/pr-${PR_NUMBER}"
          gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json number,title,body,url,state,labels \
            -q '{key: ("pr-" + (.number|tostring)), number: .number,
                 title: .title, body: .body, url: .url, state: .state,
                 labels: [.labels[].name]}' \
            > "input/pr-${PR_NUMBER}/ticket.json"
          gh pr view "$PR_NUMBER" --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --json title,body -q '.title, .body' > input/ticket.md
          echo "input/ticket.md: $(wc -l < input/ticket.md) lines"

      - name: Mark machine job started (issue task list)
        # Deterministic start marker in the issue body — survives agent
        # crashes/timeouts because the DONE twin below runs on always().
        # Contract: a "## Machine jobs" section with one task-list line per
        # factory run; the line's run URL is the unique id used to flip it.
        # PR-anchored runs skip it: no issue body to carry the task list.
        if: inputs.pr == ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
          NUMBER: ${{ inputs.issue }}
          JOB_LEG: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.kind }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          leg="${JOB_LEG:-dev} ($(basename "${RUNNER:-agent}" .json))"
          line="- [ ] ▶ ${leg} · [run](${RUN_URL}) · started $(date -u '+%H:%M') ⏳"
          gh issue view "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --json body -q .body > /tmp/issue_body.md
          # Collapse trailing blank lines first: body rewrites (jq raw
          # output, earlier appends, agent edits) can leave trailing
          # newlines, and a marker appended after them splits the GitHub
          # task list into separate lists (broken formatting). "$(cat …)"
          # strips ALL trailing newlines; printf adds exactly one back.
          printf '%s\n' "$(cat /tmp/issue_body.md)" > /tmp/issue_body.md
          if grep -q '^## Machine jobs' /tmp/issue_body.md; then
            printf '%s\n' "$line" >> /tmp/issue_body.md
          else
            printf '\n## Machine jobs\n%s\n' "$line" >> /tmp/issue_body.md
          fi
          gh issue edit "$NUMBER" --repo "$repo" --body-file /tmp/issue_body.md
          echo "job marker added: $line"

      - name: Run agent (fa provider via runner env overrides)
        id: run_agent
        # Hard cap under the job's 260 min: a hung agent session must FAIL
        # the leg (the always() post-actions then run inside the remaining
        # budget and the red path re-queues) instead of the job-level
        # timeout killing everything mid-post-action. NOT 45: a real fix is
        # a 40-80 minute session (gh-623 was killed mid-work at exactly 61).
        # NOT 110: dev legs over Flutter sources run the analyzer + the
        # full flutter test suite — fa gh-1077 was killed mid-work at
        # exactly 110 (live flutter_tester orphans at teardown, PR step
        # never reached) — 2026-09-30.
        timeout-minutes: 240
        env:
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUNNER: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.runner }}
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          # AI_TEAMMATE_CONFIG_FILE rides GITHUB_ENV from the resolve step
          # (pack launch.json wins, legacy tree fallback).
          AI_TEAMMATE_DISPLAY_KEY: GH-${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          AI_TEAMMATE_CONCURRENCY_KEY: ${{ needs.guard.outputs.anchor }}
          ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # Agent-pack registry base (dm.ai #579): runners may parent packs
          # by REGISTRY ref (`pr_review@latest`) — the resolver reads the
          # releases base (incl. catalog.json) from this env. Callers set
          # the repo VARIABLE to their pinned dmtools-agents release tag;
          # unset (or empty) keeps the previous file-only behavior and the
          # resolver fails with an explicit "no pack registry" error.
          DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY: ${{ vars.DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY }}
          # gh operations inside the session must act AS the SOURCE account:
          # events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger workflows.
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
        run: |
          # #542 mechanical guard: interpose the git push/commit guard shim at
          # the FRONT of PATH before `dmtools run` so EVERY push path in the
          # session is covered — both the fa agent's own shell tool (inherits
          # the dmtools process env) and the JS pre/post-actions'
          # cli_execute_command (PATH-resolved `git`). Refuses pushes to
          # main/master/default branch and closing keywords in commit
          # messages. Deliberately NOT written to $GITHUB_PATH: later workflow
          # steps (session-branch persistence) push legitimately.
          GIT_GUARD_BIN="${RUNNER_TEMP:-/tmp}/git-push-guard-bin"
          mkdir -p "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}"
          GUARD="${RUNNER_TEMP}/factory-kit/kit/git-push-guard.sh"
          [ -f "$GUARD" ] || GUARD="${FACTORY_ROOT}/scripts/git-push-guard.sh"
          ln -sf "$GUARD" "${GIT_GUARD_BIN}/git"

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),

# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus

name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&

    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:

      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
      flutter-version: ''  # JS/configs repo — dmtools & fa CLIs are prebuilt; no Flutter toolchain needed

blocks.text:
# Machine Loop Factory — Integration Guide

How to install the AI development factory (dev → PR → CI → review → merge,
fully autonomous, human only files issues) into a GitHub repository using
dmtools + dmtools-agents. This is the exact setup running on
`epam/dmtools-dart`; the same recipe ports any repo, including non-dmtools
projects.

---

## 1. What you get

```
            ┌──────────────────────── the loop ────────────────────────┐
 issue with  │                                                          │
 agent:dev ──┤  dev leg ──► PR ──► CI (quality) ──► review leg ──┬─► APPROVE ─► merge ─► issue closed
             │   (fa)                (GitHub Actions)   (fa+kimi  │
             │                          │ red?           queue)   └─► CHANGES ─► rework leg ─┐
             │                          ▼                                              │
             │                    rework leg ◄───────────────────────────────────────────┘
             └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 SM watchdog (cron */10, deterministic, no LLM): sees dead letters, stale
 labels, review-ready PRs, approved PRs → dispatches the right leg, merges
 (FIFO, 1 per tick), recovers stuck cycles.
```

Design invariants:

- **The tracker is the state machine.** GitHub issue labels + PR facts are
  the single source of truth. No SM-side database: every tick re-derives
  state from the API (level-triggered controller — a lost event cannot
  corrupt the loop; the next tick heals it).
- **Two state carriers**: an issue (the normal case — label lifecycle on
  the issue, the linked PR enriches observations like `prChecks`), or a PR
  alone (`type: 'pr'` rules — for PRs born without an issue).
- **SM is deterministic** (JSRunner, no LLM): the loop can always converge
  even when every AI leg is down.

---

## 2. Components

| Component | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **factory/teammate.yml** | **dmtools-agents** (`.github/workflows/factory/`, reusable) | the legs: `guard → dev/review/rework` jobs, dmtools + `fa` agent |
| **factory/sm.yml** | **dmtools-agents** (reusable) | SM watchdog tick: rules → reconcile |
| thin stubs (~15 lines each) | target repo `.github/workflows/` | ONLY triggers + concurrency + `uses:` call |
| `smAgent.js` + `sm/` | dmtools-agents (`js/smAgent.js`, `js/sm/sources/`, `js/common/smProvider.js`) | engine: rules → state query → dispatch/local execution |
| `sm_github.json` | dmtools-agents (repo root) | default GitHub rule pack |
| runners (`fa-*.json`) | dmtools-agents (`configs/runners/`) | per-leg agent configs (prompts, models, timers) |
| `.dmtools/config.js` | target repo root | repo-specific overrides (rules, repository, workflow names) |
| `merge-trigger.yml` | target repo (optional fast-path) | merges on `pr_approved` + green main (`workflow_run` cannot live in a reusable) |
| `auto-update-prs.yml` | target repo (optional) | blanket branch updates — see §9 before enabling |

The factory workflows are **reusable** (`workflow_call`): they execute in
the CALLER's context — `github.repository`, `vars.*` and `secrets.*`
resolve from the target repo, and the engine is self-pinned via
`github.workflow_ref` (runners/scripts always match the invoked ref). The
dmtools CLI installs from its release asset (version-locked), so the
target repo needs no copies of anything.

---

## 3. Prerequisites

### 3.1 Repo settings
- **Branch protection on `main`, strict**: required checks = your quality
  workflow's jobs; require branches up to date. The machine only merges
  `CLEAN` PRs, so protection defines "ready".
- Actions → Allow all actions (or allowlist `dmtools`, `sub-mod`, `ephm`).

### 3.2 Secrets (repo or org)

| Secret | Used by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` | ai-teammate legs, auto-update | **PAT of the machine account** (not the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`): labels added with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not fire `issues:` events (#116 lesson), and bot pushes must not be `github-actions[bot]` (non-collaborator → runs land in `action_required`). |
| `PAT_TOKEN` | auto-update (first choice) | owner PAT; pushes with it definitely trigger downstream CI |
| `ZAI_CODE_KEY` | dev/rework legs | z.ai API key (glm) |
| `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY` | review leg | kimi API key |

### 3.3 Variables (repo or org)

| Var | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `FA_VERSION_MACHINE` | `v0.1.392` | pins the `fa` CLI for the machine; falls back `FA_VERSION` (org) → `latest` |
| `DMTOOLS_VERSION` | `v0.1.14` | pins the dmtools CLI release bundle the workflows install |
| `FLUTTER_VERSION` | `stable` | Flutter SDK for agent work, cached per version (flutter-action). Empty string opts out — pure-Dart targets get `dart` from the runner image |
| `SM_AGENTS_REF` | `<sha>` | pin of dmtools-agents the SM uses (a branch **hash**, not a mutable ref) |
| `MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED` | `true` | fuse for merge-trigger.yml |

### 3.4 dmtools.env (repo root, git-ignored) — for local runs
```
SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN=<pat>
SOURCE_GITHUB_WORKSPACE=<owner>
SOURCE_GITHUB_REPOSITORY=<repo>
DMTOOLS_TRACKER_REPO=<owner>/<repo>
DEFAULT_TRACKER=github
```
CI gets the same values from secrets/vars; the file is only for local
dry runs of the engine.

---

## 4. Step-by-step integration

### Step 1 — workflows (two thin stubs)
Drop these into the target repo `.github/workflows/` — nothing else:

```yaml
# factory-teammate.yml
name: 'AI Teammate'
on:
  issues: { types: [assigned, labeled] }
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue: { description: Issue number, required: true, type: number }
      leg: { description: 'dev | review | rework (empty = derive)', required: false, type: string }
concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  factory:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@main
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ inputs.leg || '' }}
    secrets: inherit
```

```yaml
# factory-sm.yml
name: 'Machine SM'
on:
  schedule: [{ cron: '*/10 * * * *' }]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun: { description: Log only, required: false, type: boolean, default: true }
concurrency:
  group: machine-sm
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  sm:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@main
    with:
      dryRun: ${{ inputs.dryRun || false }}
    secrets: inherit
```

Pin `@main` to a tag/sha of dmtools-agents for production (the factory
version then moves in lockstep with the engine).

### Step 2 — rules
Start from `configs/sm_github.json`. The default pack encodes the loop:

```jsonc
[
  // red CI + agent:rework label, no run in flight → rework leg
  { "description": "red CI → rework",
    "source": "github",
    "query": { "type": "issue", "labels": ["agent:rework"], "prChecks": "red" },
    "configFile": "configs/runners/fa-rework-zai.json" },

  // dev finished (ai_developed), PR green, not yet reviewed → review leg
  { "description": "green after dev → review",
    "query": { "type": "issue", "labels": ["ai_developed"],
               "notLabels": ["ai_pr_reviewed"], "prChecks": "green" },
    "configFile": "configs/runners/fa-review-kimi.json" },

  // approved + green + mergeable → merge, oldest first, one per tick
  { "description": "approved → merge (FIFO, 1/tick)",
    "query": { "type": "pr", "labels": ["pr_approved"],
               "checks": "green", "mergeable": true },
    "configFile": "configs/retry_merge_github.json",
    "localExecution": true, "limit": 1 }
]
```

Repo-specific tuning goes to `.dmtools/config.js` in the target repo:

```js
module.exports = {
  machineSm: {
    repository: { owner: 'epam', repo: 'dmtools-dart' },
    workflowFile: 'ai-teammate.yml',
    workflowBudget: { maxWorkflows: 1 },
    rules: [ /* full rules or per-description overrides */ ]
  }
};
```

### Step 3 — labels
The pack relies on this taxonomy (all configurable via rules):

| Label | Set by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `agent:dev` / `agent:review` / `agent:rework` | human / SM | leg request (dead-letter safe: SM re-fires) |
| `ai_developed` | dev leg | PR exists, hands to r…

- `FLUTTER_VERSION` (repo/org var): "Flutter SDK for agent work, cached per version (flutter-action). Empty string opts out — pure-Dart targets get `dart` from the runner image"

The PR adds a workflow input `flutter-version: ''` to the `uses:` call. But is `flutter-version` actually a valid input of the pinned `factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006`?
